testingFeedback: 22 issues found by automated tests and integration reviews; all fixed and recorded with regressions in docs/testing.md.
3 critical/game-breaking issues: disposal discarded results, a Hub terminal-state restart, and recursive overlay Back navigation. All fixed.
The ordinary-control full campaign playthrough: fresh training through all three disposals, recovery, diagnosis, fire and credits, with no developer state writes.
The initial title-only smoke check had the least gameplay coverage; it was useful mainly for loading and visual composition.
engineFeedback: Native shaded pixel assets, Humanoid rigs and the controller Shell work together in one renderer.

I initially assumed physical pause always called game.pause(), underestimated buffer-versus-CSS scaling on dense phones, and misused the custom Back callback. Source inspection and focused regressions corrected each.
The authoritative deterministic repair/evidence simulation, seeded content validator and cooperative transport adapters.
Coordinating native fixed steps and menus with online wall-clock authority, cancelable holds and audiovisual lifecycle.
None. The engine is unmodified; game-owned shapes, materials, poses, instruments, settings, screens and input hooks extend its existing APIs.
A single documented pause/lifecycle notification covering physical buttons, menu calls, blur and controller loss would simplify integration.
promptFeedback: The primary-source references and concrete completion gates kept the repair, deduction and verification goals clear.
TASK owns naming while PLAN describes a full campaign and a shorter Hub dispatch; those required separate explicit configurations.
Keeping touch-assisted holds, native pause, cooperative authority and stencil deduction consistent through the same repair rules.
Add a compact machine-readable acceptance schema and fixed module contracts beside the prose; retain the explicit unavailable-hardware boundaries.

aiHub.name: Bomb Union
aiHub.description: Clock in with a municipal bomb-disposal crew, repair hazardous circuits and read the stencil evidence they reveal. Work solo or share sectors with up to four technicians, then deliberately commit to the disarm code.
aiHub.controls: D-pad/WASD/mouse/tap targets; Cross/Space apply; L1/R1 or 1–4 tools; Square/E test; Triangle/R repeat; R2/Tab evidence; Options/Escape menu.
